correctness.rationale: For a shattered set of size at least three, full-trace realization confines every parameter to distance two from a common witness. A distance-four pair has a unique midpoint and cannot realize its pair-only trace, forcing all pairwise distances two and a common tree center. A complete local classification of distance-two traces from the common neighbor then yields exactly the outward-deep/extra-neighbor criterion, excludes all four-shattering, and counts triples uniquely. Three separate outward length-two paths plus an extra center neighbor force eleven distinct vertices, attained explicitly. A separate standard-library verifier checks 18,889 finite trees, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact center-degree formula for a natural model-theoretic shattering invariant on every finite tree, a sharp VC bound, and a sharp minimum universe size. It separates exact-radius spheres from classical radius-at-most balls and supports computable counts in linear time by local depth inspection; these claims are not arbitrary numerical slices or immediate restatements of generic type-counting bounds.
